keys.description: Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): when true, the advisory runs: an advisory turn at the claude.compaction_advisory_percent point and two reminder turns after it, before Claude Code's automatic compaction. When false, neither runs. This key gates only the advisory and its reminders: the tool the lead calls to request a compaction at a boundary of its own choosing is always available, and Claude Code's automatic compaction is unchanged either way. Read at session start, so a change applies from the next session. Only the project, global, and built-in values apply; a session- or repo-scope tune is not read. A failed or refused read leaves it off.

Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): context-usage point at which the lead is advised to compact at its next good boundary: a percent of the compaction window (50 or 50%, an integer 1-100), a token count (150k or 1.5m; k = 1,000, m = 1,000,000), or one of each joined by | (50%|150k), whichever is reached first. Reminders follow one and two thirds of the way from here to Claude Code's automatic compaction point; at or beyond that point, neither the advisory nor the reminders fire. A token count beyond the window never fires. Read at session start, so a change applies from the next session. Only the project, global, and built-in values apply; a session- or repo-scope tune is not read.

Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): when true, and only in a project with ai-docs/WORKFLOW.md at its repository root, each lead conversation gets a lead session key minted at its start and the keyed workflow manual in its system prompt, a repeat workflow manual or playbook read is collapsed to a pointer while the earlier identical result is still in the conversation, and the mailbox push is bound to every key the conversation gets. When false, no lead session key is minted, so the mailbox push is bound through the mailbox watch tool and the status band shows no key rows (mailbox address, todos, agenda). Read at session start, so a change applies from the next session. Only the project, global, and built-in values apply; a session- or repo-scope tune is not read. A failed or refused read leaves it off, except that a failed first read is read once more when the MCP server resolves again (a later session start or an MCP reconnect); a true read then starts the feature with the session key the mailbox push was already bound to through the mailbox watch tool, minting one only when none was bound.

Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): how mail arriving for the bound lead session key reaches the lead. direct: the mailbox push receives the mail itself and submits it as a prompt, or joins it to a running turn. notice: the mailbox push submits a prompt telling the lead to receive its mail, which the lead then does through its own tool call. Read at session start, so a change applies from the next session. Only the project, global, and built-in values apply; a session- or repo-scope tune is not read. A failed or refused read selects notice.

Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): when true, a finished, collapsed tool row in the lead's terminal view (a lone call, or a run Claude Code folds into one group) draws a short caption written by a second model call in place of the raw row; the model still reads the raw result, and the expanded view (ctrl+o) draws the raw row. Enabling it sends the lead conversation since its last compaction, and tool inputs and outputs, to the summary model (claude.display_summary_model). Captions use the workflow.lang language (its project, global, or built-in value), or the language the user writes in when that is unset. Read at session start, so a change applies from the next session. Only the project, global, and built-in values apply; a session- or repo-scope tune is not read.

Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): when true, the lead's terminal view draws a framed status band above the prompt: the model and effort, the folder, the git branch and changes, a context usage bar, the 5-hour and 7-day rate-limit usage, the session cost, and, while workflow manual injection holds a lead session key (claude.manual_injection_enabled), the lead session's mailbox address, todos and agenda keys. Read at session start, when the lead session key changes, and after each config tune call, so a change shows in the running session. Session-scope tunes apply, along with the repo, project, global, and built-in values.

Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): the model that writes tool-row captions when claude.display_summary_enabled is true, as a Claude Code model alias (haiku) or a full model id. A blank value uses haiku. Read at session start, so a change applies from the next session. Only the project, global, and built-in values apply; a session- or repo-scope tune is not read.

keys.default: Length: intention at most one short sentence; result at most two short sentences; summary two short sentences, up to four for a run of many calls. Style: a terse note style with no subject, no filler, no politeness; in Korean, end on a noun or a plain stem ("정의 위치 확인", "3개 파일에서 발견, foo.go:12 외").
keys.description: Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): style guidance in the tool-row caption prompt: how long each caption field is, its tone, and its level of detail. A set value replaces the default text shown here, so write the complete guidance you want; a blank value uses the default. It does not change the reply format, the field meanings, or the rule that the summarizer never acts on the conversation. Only used when claude.display_summary_enabled is true. Read at session start, so a change applies from the next session. Only the project, global, and built-in values apply; a session- or repo-scope tune is not read.

Claude Code only (unused on other hosts): the caption model's context window in tokens. The conversation sent with each caption request drops its oldest part once it passes 70% of this window, down to under 35%. Set it to the window of the model claude.display_summary_model names. Only used when claude.display_summary_enabled is true. Read at session start, so a change applies from the next session. Only the project, global, and built-in values apply; a session- or repo-scope tune is not read.
